112	_usage() {
113	    # Usage shown on error or --help. Unix convention: stderr (#619).
114	    cat >&2 <<EOF
115	Usage: runner.sh --issue <N>|--goal "<text>" [--dry-run] [--template <id>]
116	                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
117	  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
118	  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
119	  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
120	  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
121	  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
122	  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
123	  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
124	                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
125	                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
126	  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
127	  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
128	                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)
129	
130	Environment:
131	  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
132	  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
133	  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
134	  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.
135	EOF
136	}
137	
138	# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
139	#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
140	#   write_scope_override
141	#   _update_stage_status         } → core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh
142	#   _set_pipeline_status
143	#   (+ their _zbuild_runner_set_* jq filter helpers)
144	
145	# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
146	_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
147	# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
148	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
149	_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""
150	
151	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
152	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
153	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
154	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
155	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
156	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
157	_runner_retry_budget() {
158	    local v=""
159	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
161	    fi
162	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
163	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
164	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
165	    printf '%s' "$v"
166	}
167	
168	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
169	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
170	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
171	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
172	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
173	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
174	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
175	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
176	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
177	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
178	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
179	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
180	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
181	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
182	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
184	    _runner_ended=true
185	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
186	    return 0
187	}
188	
189	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
190	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
191	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
192	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
193	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
194	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
195	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
196	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
197	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
198	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
199	    case "$v" in
200	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
201	        *) return 1 ;;
202	    esac
203	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
204	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
205	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
206	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
207	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
208	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
209	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
210	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
211	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
212	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
213	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
215	    _runner_ended=true
216	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
217	    return 0
218	}
219	
220	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
221	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
222	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
223	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
224	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
225	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
226	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
227	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
228	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
229	    local latest="" n=0 d k
230	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
231	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
232	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
233	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
234	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
235	    done
236	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
237	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
238	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
239	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
240	        return
241	    fi
242	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
243	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
244	}
245	
246	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
247	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
248	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
249	_runner_note_push_failure() {
250	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
251	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
252	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
253	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
254	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
255	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
256	}
257	
258	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
259	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
260	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
261	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. Only when HEAD carries
262	# commits past the intake baseline. Advisory: a failure is reported, never fatal.
263	_runner_push_work_branch() {
264	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
265	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
266	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
267	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
268	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
269	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
270	    local _base=""
271	    [[ -f "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" ]] && _base="$(cat "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)"
272	    if [[ -n "$_base" ]]; then
273	        local _ahead; _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
274	        [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
275	    fi
276	    local _err
277	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
278	        return 0
279	    fi
280	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
281	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
282	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
283	    return 0
284	}
285	
286	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
287	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
288	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
289	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
290	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
291	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
292	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
293	    local _sd="${1:-}" _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch=""
294	    [[ -f "$_sd/intake-branch.txt" ]] && read -r _branch 2>/dev/null < "$_sd/intake-branch.txt"
295	    _branch="${_branch//[[:space:]]/}"
296	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
297	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
298	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
299	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
300	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
301	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
302	        reattached)
303	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
304	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
305	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
306	        diverged)
307	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
308	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
309	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
310	    esac
311	    return 0
312	}
313	
314	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
315	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
316	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
317	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
318	# never blocks a run.
319	#
320	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
321	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
322	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
323	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
324	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
325	# item 1 of #1807.
326	#
327	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
328	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
329	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
330	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
331	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
332	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
333	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
334	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
335	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
336	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
337	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
338	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
339	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
340	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
341	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
342	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
343	    # push had nothing to send.
344	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
345	
346	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
347	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
348	        saved)
349	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
350	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
351	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
352	            ;;
353	        failed)
354	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
355	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
356	            # no channel to surface on.
357	            #
358	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
359	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
360	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
361	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
362	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
363	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
364	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
365	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
366	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
367	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
368	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
369	            fi
370	            ;;
371	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
372	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
373	        *) : ;;
374	    esac
375	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
376	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
377	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
378	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
379	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
380	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
381	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
382	    local _leak=""
383	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
384	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
385	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
386	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
387	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
388	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
389	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
390	        return 0
391	    fi
392	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
393	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
394	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
395	    fi
396	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
397	    return 0
398	}

467	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
468	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
469	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
470	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
471	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
472	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
473	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""

475	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
476	        local i
477	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
478	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
479	            sleep 0.1
480	        done
481	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
482	    fi
483	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true

487	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
488	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
489	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
490	_runner_now_short() {
491	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
492	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
493	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
494	        return 0
495	    fi
496	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
497	    local out
498	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
499	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \

504	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
505	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
506	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
507	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
508	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
509	_runner_duration_token() {
510	    local stage="$1"
511	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
512	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
513	        printf '?s'
514	        return 0
515	    fi
516	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
517	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
518	        printf '?s'
519	        return 0
520	    fi
521	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
522	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
523	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
524	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
525	    else
526	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
527	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
528	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
529	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
530	    fi
531	}

567	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
568	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
569	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
570	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
571	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
572	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
573	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
574	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
575	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
576	_runner_record_report() {
577	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
578	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
579	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
580	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
581	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
582	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
583	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
584	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
585	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
586	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
587	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
588	        sleep 0.05
589	    done
590	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
591	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
592	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
593	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
594	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
595	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
596	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
597	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
598	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
599	    else
600	        rm -f "$tmp"
601	    fi
602	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
603	    return 0
604	}

606	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
607	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
608	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
609	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
610	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
611	#
612	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
613	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
614	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
615	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
616	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
617	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
618	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
619	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
620	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
621	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
622	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
623	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
624	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
625	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
626	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
627	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
628	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
629	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
630	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
631	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
632	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
633	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
634	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
635	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
636	        return 1
637	    fi
638	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
639	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
640	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
641	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
642	        return 1
643	    fi
644	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
645	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
646	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
647	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
648	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
649	    #
650	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
651	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
652	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
653	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
654	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
655	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
656	    #
657	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
658	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
659	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
660	    #
661	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
662	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
663	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
664	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
665	    fi
666	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
667	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
668	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
669	    # an unchanged tree.
670	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
671	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
672	    fi
673	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
674	    local _leaf _ok=1
675	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
676	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
677	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
678	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
679	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
680	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
681	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
682	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
683	        esac
684	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
685	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
686	            _ok=0
687	        fi
688	    done
689	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
690	}

692	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
693	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
694	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
695	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
696	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
697	#
698	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
699	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
700	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
701	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
702	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
703	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
704	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
705	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
706	#
707	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
708	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
709	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
710	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
711	#
712	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
713	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
714	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
715	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
716	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
717	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
718	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
719	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
720	_runner_template_personas() {
721	    awk '
722	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
723	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
724	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
725	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
726	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
727	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
728	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
729	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
730	        }
731	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
732	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
733	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
734	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
735	        }
736	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
737	}

739	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
740	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
741	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
742	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
743	    case "$mode" in
744	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
745	        *) mode="warn" ;;
746	    esac
747	
748	    # off = complete no-op, no output
749	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
750	
751	    local -a violations=()
752	    local fail_count=0
753	
754	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
755	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
756	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
757	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
758	    fi
759	
760	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
761	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
762	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
763	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
764	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
765	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
766	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
767	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
768	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
769	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
770	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
771	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
772	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
773	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
774	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
775	    fi
776	
777	    # No violations → clean
778	    [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]] && return 0
779	
780	    # Render all violations in a single block (render-all-at-once pattern).
781	    # #1826 moved the loop itself into _inputs_render_violations so the
782	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
783	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
784	    _inputs_render_violations \
785	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
786	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
787	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
788	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
789	        "${violations[@]}"
790	
791	    # Emit event (best-effort)
792	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
793	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
794	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
795	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
796	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
797	    fi
798	
799	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
800	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
801	        return 0
802	    fi
803	
804	    # enforce: fail-closed
805	    return 1
806	}

832	# Parallel to _runner_duration_token but for the pipeline-wide window. No stage
833	# argument — reads _RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS directly. Returns "?s" on cache
834	# miss so the banner still renders during very-early failures.
835	_runner_pipeline_duration_token() {
836	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"
837	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
838	        printf '?s'
839	        return 0
840	    fi
841	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
842	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
843	        printf '?s'
844	        return 0
845	    fi
846	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
847	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
848	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
849	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
850	    else
851	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
852	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
853	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
854	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"

896	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
897	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
898	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
899	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
900	#
901	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
902	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
903	#
904	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
905	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
906	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
907	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
908	#
909	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
910	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
911	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
912	# against banner-write failures.
913	_render_pipeline_end() {
914	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
915	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
916	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
917	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
918	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
919	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
920	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
921	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
922	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
923	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
924	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
925	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
926	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
927	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
928	    # (#1156)
929	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
930	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
931	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
932	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
933	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
934	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
935	
936	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
937	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
938	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
939	    local word
940	    case "$status" in
941	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
942	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
943	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
944	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
945	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
946	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
947	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
948	    esac
949	
950	    local label=" pipeline.end "
951	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
952	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
953	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
954	
955	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
956	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
957	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
958	
959	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
960	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
961	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
962	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
963	        local bar
964	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
965	        bar="${bar// /═}"
966	        {
967	            printf '\n'
968	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
969	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
970	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
971	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
972	        } >&2
973	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
974	        return 0
975	    fi
976	
977	    local lbar rbar
978	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
979	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
980	    {
981	        printf '\n'
982	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
983	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
984	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
985	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
986	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
987	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
988	    } >&2
989	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
990	}

1007	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1008	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1009	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1010	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1011	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1012	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1013	#
1014	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1015	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1016	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1017	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1018	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1019	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1020	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1021	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1022	_render_stage_divider() {
1023	    local stage="$1"
1024	    local width
1025	    width="$(_term_width)"
1026	    local color
1027	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1028	    local label=" ${stage} "
1029	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1030	
1031	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1032	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1033	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1034	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1035	
1036	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1037	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1038	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1039	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1040	        local bar
1041	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1042	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1043	        {
1044	            printf '\n'
1045	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1046	            printf '\n'
1047	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1048	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1049	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1050	            printf '\n'
1051	        } >&2
1052	        return 0
1053	    fi
1054	
1055	    local lbar rbar
1056	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1057	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1058	    {
1059	        printf '\n'
1060	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1061	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1062	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1063	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1064	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1065	        printf '\n'
1066	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1067	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1068	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1069	        printf '\n'
1070	    } >&2
1071	}

1073	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1074	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1075	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1076	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1077	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1078	#
1079	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1080	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1081	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1082	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1083	#
1084	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1085	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1086	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1087	#     banner=best-effort).
1088	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1089	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1090	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1091	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1092	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1093	#
1094	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1095	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1096	
1097	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1098	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1099	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1100	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1101	_render_cycle_entry() {
1102	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1103	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1104	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1105	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1106	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1107	    local bar
1108	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1109	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1110	    {
1111	        printf '\n'
1112	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1113	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1114	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1115	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1116	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1117	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1118	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1119	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1120	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1121	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1122	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1123	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1124	        fi
1125	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1126	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1127	        printf '\n'
1128	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1129	}

1177	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1178	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1179	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1180	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1181	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1182	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1183	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1184	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1185	    local label
1186	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1187	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1188	    else
1189	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1190	    fi
1191	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1192	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1193	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1194	    local bar
1195	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1196	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1197	    {
1198	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1199	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1200	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1201	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1202	}
1203	
1204	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1205	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1206	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1207	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1208	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1209	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1210	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1211	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1212	    {
1213	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1214	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1215	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1216	}
1217	
1218	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1219	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1220	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1221	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1222	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1223	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1224	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD
1225	#   aborted         → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
1226	#   verdict_missing → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
1227	#   blocked         → ✗ RED+BOLD (sibling #528)

24	# roster. Membership is enforced by the manifest-derived resolvability preflight
25	# (_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability, runner.sh — every leaf must resolve to a
26	# plugin) and order by the upstream-input data-dependency DAG (contract-validator.sh).
27	# The retired _ZBUILD_CANONICAL_STAGES array + ZBUILD_LEGACY_STAGE_VALIDATION
28	# kill-switch (the strangler escape hatch) are deleted; the preflight + DAG are the

32	_TPL_DEFAULT_STRATEGY="fanout"
33	_TPL_MERGE_POLICY="auto_unless_flagged"
34	_TPL_STAGES=()
35	# #1831: ordered stage ids that run on EVERY exit path (success, non-zero rc,
36	# SIGINT, SIGTERM, timeout). Declared by the template's top-level `always_run:`
37	# list, NOT part of _TPL_STAGES[] — an always-run stage is not in the flow.
38	_TPL_ALWAYS_RUN=()
39	# ADR-021 (#512): list of dispatch units in template order. Each entry is
40	# "stage:<id>" or "cycle:<id>". Empty `cycles:` block → every unit is "stage:<id>"
41	# (backwards-compat — runner behavior identical to today).

44	_TPL_CYCLES=()
45	# ADR-039 (#1130): list of parallel group ids declared in template (in
46	# declaration order). Sibling of _TPL_CYCLES — a `type: parallel` group folds
47	# to one "parallel:<gid>" dispatch unit. Template-layer parse/validate only;
48	# execution lands in a later issue.

51	# declaration order). A `type: map` group folds to one "map:<gid>" dispatch unit.

123	    _TPL_STAGES=()

126	    _TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS=()

174	        [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
175	        sid="${row%%|*}"

181	    local -a collected_ids=()
182	    local -a collected_io_dests=()
183	    local -a collected_io_tail=()
184	    local -a collected_io_redact=()
185	    local -a collected_router_timeout=()

187	    local -a collected_router_max_iterations=()
188	    local -a collected_router_retries=()

206	                collected_io_dests+=("$s_iod")
207	                collected_io_tail+=("$s_iot")
208	                collected_io_redact+=("$s_ior")
209	                collected_router_timeout+=("$s_rt")
210	                collected_router_max_turns+=("$s_rmt")
211	                collected_router_max_iterations+=("$s_rmi")
212	                collected_router_retries+=("$s_rre")
213	                stage_data_rows+=("$s_id|$s_roles|$s_strat|$s_iod|$s_iot|$s_ior|$s_rt|$s_rmt|$s_rmi|$s_rre")

215	            IC)

217	                # <cid>|<cstages>|<cmax>|<conmax>|<custage>|<cufield>|<cuop>|<cuvalue>|<cplateau>|<cdiverg>|<cvelopl>|<cdesc>
218	                # #831: cdesc is the optional operator-facing description.

221	                # pipe field separator). Absent block ⇒ safe defaults below.

223	                local cexpand cautogrant cescalate condeny
224	                IFS='|' read -r cid cstages cmax conmax custage cufield cuop cuvalue cplateau cdiverg cvelopl cdesc cexpand cautogrant cescalate condeny <<< "$payload"

226	                _TPL_CYCLES+=("$cid")
227	                local safe="${cid//-/_}"
228	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}"        '%s' "$cstages"
229	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_MAX_${safe}"           '%s' "$cmax"
230	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_ON_MAX_${safe}"        '%s' "${conmax:-continue}"
231	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_UNOWNED_${safe}"       '%s' ""
232	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_${safe}"   '%s' "$custage"
233	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_${safe}"   '%s' "$cufield"
234	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_${safe}"      '%s' "$cuop"
235	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_${safe}"   '%s' "$cuvalue"
236	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_PLATEAU_W_${safe}"            '%s' "$cplateau"
237	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_W_${safe}"         '%s' "$cdiverg"
238	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_W_${safe}"   '%s' "$cvelopl"
239	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_DESCRIPTION_${safe}"          '%s' "${cdesc:-}"

241	                # not expandable ⇒ governed-deny ⇒ clean abandon).
242	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_EXPANDABLE_${safe}" '%s' "${cexpand:-false}"
243	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_AUTO_GRANT_${safe}" '%s' "${cautogrant:-}"
244	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ESCALATE_${safe}"   '%s' "${cescalate:-none}"
245	                printf -v "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ON_DENY_${safe}"    '%s' "${condeny:-abandon}"
246	                export "_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_MAX_${safe}" \
247	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_ON_MAX_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_STAGE_${safe}" \
248	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_FIELD_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_OP_${safe}" \
249	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_UNTIL_VALUE_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_PLATEAU_W_${safe}" \
250	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_DIVERGENCE_W_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_VELOCITY_PLATEAU_W_${safe}" \
251	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_DESCRIPTION_${safe}" \
252	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_EXPANDABLE_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_AUTO_GRANT_${safe}" \
253	                       "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ESCALATE_${safe}" "_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_ON_DENY_${safe}"
254	                # Expand cycle members in order into the flat stage list.
255	                local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
256	                # shellcheck disable=SC2206
257	                local -a members=($cstages)
258	                IFS="$IFS_save"
259	                local m m_row m_roles m_strat m_iod m_iot m_ior m_rt m_rmt m_rmi m_rre
260	                # Dedupe set: stage ids already added to _TPL_STAGES via a
261	                # prior IC| row in the same template (nested-cycle case).
262	                # Without this a parent cycle re-adds its descendant cycle's
263	                # members and breaks the canonical-order validator.
264	                for m in "${members[@]}"; do
265	                    # ADR-027 (Wave 17-B): cycle-as-member. If `m` is itself
266	                    # a known cycle (registered by an earlier IC| row from
267	                    # the translator topo pre-pass), recursively expand its
268	                    # member list into the flat _TPL_STAGES[] view rather
269	                    # than treating `m` as a leaf stage id (cycle ids are

993	    ' "$file"
994	}
995	
996	# ─── _tpl_parse_stage_definitions — parse `stage_definitions:` map (v2) ─────
997	# Emits one S|<id>|<roles>|<strategy>|<io_dests>|<io_tail>|<io_redact>|<rt>|<rmt>|<rmi>
998	# row per definition. Same payload shape as _tpl_parse_stage_data so the load
999	# pipeline can consume both streams uniformly.
1000	_tpl_parse_stage_definitions() {
1001	    local file="$1"
1002	    awk '
1003	    function trim(s) { sub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", s); sub(/[[:space:]]+$/, "", s); return s }
1004	    function flush_def() {
1005	        if (cur_id == "")
1006	            return
1007	        print cur_id "|" cur_roles "|" cur_strategy "|" cur_io_dests "|" cur_io_tail "|" cur_io_redact "|" cur_rt "|" cur_rmt "|" cur_rmi "|" cur_rre
1008	    }
1009	    function reset_def() {
1010	        cur_id = ""; cur_roles = ""; cur_strategy = ""
1011	        cur_io_dests = ""; cur_io_tail = ""; cur_io_redact = ""
1012	        cur_rt = ""; cur_rmt = ""; cur_rmi = ""; cur_rre = ""
1013	        in_roles = 0; in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 0
1014	    }
1015	    BEGIN { reset_def() }
1016	    /^stage_definitions:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_defs = 1; next }
1017	    in_defs && /^[a-zA-Z_]/ { flush_def(); reset_def(); in_defs = 0; next }
1018	    # Each top-level def is "  <id>:" (2-space indent).
1019	    in_defs && /^[[:space:]]+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:[[:space:]]*$/ {
1020	        # Distinguish "  <id>:" (indent 2) from deeper "    <field>:" (indent 4+).
1021	        line = $0
1022	        indent = match(line, /[^ ]/) - 1
1023	        if (indent == 2) {
1024	            flush_def(); reset_def()
1025	            cur_id = line; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+/, "", cur_id); gsub(/:[[:space:]]*$/, "", cur_id)
1026	            next
1027	        }
1028	    }
1029	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_roles && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
1030	        item = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", item); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", item)
1031	        if (item != "") {
1032	            if (cur_roles == "") cur_roles = item
1033	            else cur_roles = cur_roles "," item
1034	        }
1035	        next
1036	    }
1037	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_roles { in_roles = 0 }
1038	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_io_dests && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
1039	        item = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", item); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", item)
1040	        if (item != "") {
1041	            if (cur_io_dests == "") cur_io_dests = item
1042	            else cur_io_dests = cur_io_dests "," item
1043	        }
1044	        next
1045	    }
1046	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && in_io_dests { in_io_dests = 0 }
1047	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+roles:/ {
1048	        roles_line = $0
1049	        if (roles_line ~ /\[/) {
1050	            sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", roles_line)
1051	            sub(/\].*$/, "", roles_line)
1052	            gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", roles_line)
1053	            cur_roles = roles_line
1054	        } else { in_roles = 1 }
1055	        next
1056	    }
1057	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+strategy:/ {
1058	        in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 0
1059	        cur_strategy = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+strategy:[[:space:]]*/, "", cur_strategy); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", cur_strategy)
1060	        next
1061	    }
1062	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+io:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_io_block = 1; in_router_block = 0; next }
1063	    in_defs && cur_id != "" && /^[[:space:]]+router:[[:space:]]*$/ { in_io_block = 0; in_io_dests = 0; in_router_block = 1; next }
1064	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:/ {
1065	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+timeout_s:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rt = v; next
1066	    }
1067	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+max_turns:/ {
1068	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+max_turns:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rmt = v; next
1069	    }
1070	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+max_iterations:/ {
1071	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+max_iterations:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rmi = v; next
1072	    }
1073	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+retries:/ {
1074	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+retries:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_rre = v; next
1075	    }
1076	    in_defs && in_router_block && /^[[:space:]]+[a-z_]+:/ { next }
1077	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+destinations:/ {
1078	        dest_line = $0
1079	        if (dest_line ~ /\[/) {
1080	            sub(/^[^[]*\[/, "", dest_line)
1081	            sub(/\].*$/, "", dest_line)
1082	            gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", dest_line)
1083	            cur_io_dests = dest_line
1084	            in_io_dests = 0
1085	        } else { in_io_dests = 1 }
1086	        next
1087	    }
1088	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+tail_lines:/ {
1089	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+tail_lines:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_io_tail = v; in_io_dests = 0; next
1090	    }
1091	    in_defs && in_io_block && /^[[:space:]]+redact:/ {
1092	        v = $0; gsub(/^[[:space:]]+redact:[[:space:]]*/, "", v); gsub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); cur_io_redact = v; in_io_dests = 0; next
1093	    }
1094	    END { flush_def() }
1095	    ' "$file"
1096	}
1097	
1098	# ─── _tpl_validate_cycles — enforce ADR-021 invariants ───────────────────────
1099	# - stages[] is contiguous subsequence of canonical (_TPL_STAGES) order
1100	# - max_iterations integer 1..10 (REQUIRED)
1101	# - until.stage MUST be in cycle.stages
1102	# - cycles MUST NOT overlap each other
1103	_tpl_validate_cycles() {
1104	    [[ ${#_TPL_CYCLES[@]} -eq 0 ]] && return 0
1105	    local cid prev_end=-1
1106	    local -A seen_stage=()
1107	    for cid in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
1108	        local safe="${cid//-/_}"
1109	        local stages_var="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${safe}"
1110	        local stages_csv="${!stages_var:-}"
1111	        if [[ -z "$stages_csv" ]]; then
1112	            error "cycle '$cid': no stages declared"
1113	            return 1
1114	        fi
1115	        local IFS_save="$IFS"; IFS=','
1116	        # shellcheck disable=SC2206
1117	        local -a cs=($stages_csv)
1118	        IFS="$IFS_save"
1119	
1120	        # Every stage of the loop — its inner loops and parallel groups expanded
1121	        # where they sit (#2271: an outer loop's own stages may sit between its
1122	        # inner loops) — must be a known _TPL_STAGES entry, contiguous and in
1123	        # order. A stage belongs DIRECTLY to at most one loop.
1124	        local s _c _is_cyc _is_par _pg
1125	        for s in "${cs[@]}"; do
1126	            _is_cyc=0; _is_par=0
1127	            for _c in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do [[ "$_c" == "$s" ]] && { _is_cyc=1; break; }; done
1128	            for _pg in "${_TPL_PARALLEL_GROUPS[@]}"; do [[ "$_pg" == "$s" ]] && { _is_par=1; break; }; done
1129	            [[ $_is_cyc -eq 1 || $_is_par -eq 1 ]] && continue
1130	            if [[ -n "${seen_stage[$s]:-}" ]]; then
1131	                error "cycle '$cid': stage '$s' is in another cycle (cycles must not overlap)"
1132	                return 1
1133	            fi
1134	            seen_stage[$s]=1
1135	        done
1136	        local first_pos=-1 last_pos=-1 pos i
1137	        while IFS= read -r s; do
1138	            [[ -n "$s" ]] || continue
1139	            pos=-1
1140	            for i in "${!_TPL_STAGES[@]}"; do
1141	                [[ "${_TPL_STAGES[$i]}" == "$s" ]] && { pos=$i; break; }
1142	            done
1143	            if [[ $pos -eq -1 ]]; then
1144	                error "cycle '$cid': stage '$s' not in template stages[]"
1145	                return 1
1146	            fi
1147	            if [[ $first_pos -ne -1 && $pos -ne $((last_pos + 1)) ]]; then
1148	                error "cycle '$cid': stages must be a contiguous subsequence of template stages[]"
1149	                return 1
1150	            fi
1151	            [[ $first_pos -eq -1 ]] && first_pos=$pos
1152	            last_pos=$pos
1153	        done < <(_tpl_flow_leaves "$cid")
1154	
1155	        # Top-level loops must not overlap each other; a nested loop lies inside
1156	        # its outer loop's range by construction.
1157	        local _nested_in=0 _oc _ov
1158	        for _oc in "${_TPL_CYCLES[@]}"; do
1159	            _ov="_TPL_CYCLE_STAGES_${_oc//-/_}"
1160	            [[ ",${!_ov:-}," == *",$cid,"* ]] && { _nested_in=1; break; }
1161	        done
1162	        if [[ $_nested_in -eq 0 && $first_pos -ne -1 ]]; then
1163	            if [[ $first_pos -le $prev_end ]]; then
1164	                error "cycle '$cid': overlaps a previously declared cycle"
1165	                return 1
1166	            fi
1167	            prev_end=$last_pos
1168	        fi
1169	
1170	        # max_iterations required + bounded
1171	        local max_var="_TPL_CYCLE_MAX_${safe}"
1172	        local max="${!max_var:-}"
1173	        if [[ -z "$max" ]] || ! [[ "$max" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || [[ "$max" -lt 1 ]] || [[ "$max" -gt 10 ]]; then
1174	            error "cycle '$cid': max_iterations required integer in 1..10, got: ${max:-<unset>}"
1175	            return 1
1176	        fi
1177	
1178	        # #840 scope_policy enum validation (ADR-030). All fields optional;
1179	        # absent ⇒ safe defaults already applied by the consumer. When present,
1180	        # values MUST be from the closed vocabularies — the template names
1181	        # behaviors, it cannot express logic.
1182	        local sx_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_EXPANDABLE_${safe}"; local sx="${!sx_var:-false}"
1183	        if [[ "$sx" != "true" && "$sx" != "false" ]]; then
1184	            error "cycle '$cid': scope_policy.expandable must be true|false, got: $sx"
1185	            return 1
1186	        fi
1187	        local sag_var="_TPL_CYCLE_SCOPE_AUTO_GRANT_${safe}"; local sag="${!sag_var:-}"
1188	        if [[ -n "$sag" ]]; then
1189	            local _cls
1190	            local _save_ifs="$IFS"; IFS=','
1191	            # shellcheck disable=SC2206
1192	            local -a _classes=($sag)
1193	            IFS="$_save_ifs"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
3	#
4	# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
5	# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
6	# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
7	# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
8	#
9	# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
10	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
11	_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1
12	
13	if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
14	    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
15	    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
16	fi
17	
18	# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
19	# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
20	# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
21	# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
22	# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
23	#
24	# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
25	# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
26	# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
27	# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
28	_route_manifest_knob() {
29	    local knob="$1"
30	    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
31	    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
32	    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
33	    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
34	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
35	    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
36	    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
37	    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
38	    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
39	    printf '%s' "$v"
40	}
41	
42	# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
43	# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
44	# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
45	# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
46	# compile-time constant is the floor:
47	#
48	#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
49	#
50	# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
51	# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
52	# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
53	# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
54	_route_resolve_knob() {
55	    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
56	    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
57	    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
58	    local v=""
59	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
60	        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
61	    fi
62	    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
63	        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
64	        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
65	        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
66	        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
67	        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
68	        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
69	            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
70	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
71	                "env_var=$env_var" \
72	                "env_value=$env_val" \
73	                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
74	        fi
75	        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
76	    fi
77	    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
78	    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
79	        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
80	    fi
81	    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
82	        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
83	        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
84	            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
85	        fi
86	    fi
87	    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
88	}
89	
90	# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
91	# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
92	_route_resolve_timeout() {
93	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \
94	        router.timeout.override_ignored timeout_s
95	}
96	
97	# ADR-018 (#466): per-stage router.max_turns > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS > 25 default.
98	# ADR-029 G3 (#812): when the cycle orchestrator detects a router timeout for
99	# this stage, it sets ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE so the next dispatch
100	# of the same stage uses an escalated budget (+50%, capped at 2× base). The
101	# override wins over the per-stage template AND the env knob because that's
102	# the entire point — escalation must beat the static config that already
103	# proved too small.
104	_route_resolve_max_turns() {
105	    if [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
106	        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE"
107	        return 0
108	    fi
109	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_turns ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS 25 \
110	        router.max_turns.override_ignored max_turns
111	}
112	
113	# ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): when max_turns resolves to the 0 sentinel,
114	# classify which source set it (template > env > manifest > default) for
115	# telemetry. Emits `template`, `env`, `manifest` (#1816), or `default`. The
116	# `default` branch is currently unreachable (compile-time default is 25, not 0)
117	# but kept for forward compatibility if the default ever changes.
118	# Copilot review #764: compare numerically so "00", "000" etc. (accepted
119	# by the ^[0-9]+$ validator) classify correctly.
120	_route_classify_max_turns_source() {
121	    local _tpl_val=""
122	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] \
123	        && command -v template_stage_router_max_turns >/dev/null 2>&1; then
124	        _tpl_val="$(template_stage_router_max_turns "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
125	    fi
126	    local _mf_val; _mf_val="$(_route_manifest_knob max_turns)"
127	    if [[ "$_tpl_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
128	        printf '%s' "template"
129	    elif [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS}" -eq 0 ]]; then
130	        printf '%s' "env"
131	    elif [[ "$_mf_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_mf_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
132	        # #1816: a plugin that declares `max_turns: 0` owns that sentinel. Left
133	        # unclassified it would be recorded as `default`, which is the one thing
134	        # it is not — the record would name a source that declared nothing.
135	        printf '%s' "manifest"
136	    else
137	        printf '%s' "default"
138	    fi
139	}
140	
141	# ADR-018 (#467): per-stage router.max_iterations > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS > 10 default.
142	_route_resolve_max_iterations() {
143	    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_iterations ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS 10 \
144	        router.max_iterations.override_ignored
145	}
146	
147	# ADR-029 (#1230): per-stage router.retries > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES > 0 default.
148	# The count of retry-on-timeout (rc=124) attempts BEFORE the verbatim-124
149	# fallback. Default 0 (opt-in). Honored by BOTH leaf paths — single-shot
150	# (_route_call_claude) and agentic-loop (route_to_model_loop) — so every leaf
151	# node respects the knob wherever it sits. Out-of-range values (validator
152	# already bounds template 0..10; env is unbounded) clamp to 0 fail-safe.
153	_route_resolve_retries() {
154	    local v; v="$(_route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_retries ZBUILD_ROUTER_RETRIES 0 \
155	        router.retries.override_ignored retries)"
156	    if [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$v" -ge 0 ]] && [[ "$v" -le 10 ]]; then
157	        printf '%s' "$v"
158	    else
159	        printf '0'
160	    fi
161	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh — ADR-025 abort-propagation contract (Wave 15-B, #684)
3	#
4	# An abort is RECORDED once, as a word, and every dispatcher asks for it at the
5	# same two points in its loop (#1850, ADR-054 §4 — no rc carries the reason):
6	#
7	#   loop {
8	#       _zbuild_check_abort || return 1             # pre-flight
9	#       dispatch_child
10	#       _zbuild_propagate_abort $? || return 1      # post-flight
11	#   }
12	#
13	# Words: sigint | sigterm | cycle_abort | llm_unavailable | llm_rate_limited |
14	# scope_too_large. The first recorded abort wins.
15	#
16	# Two channels hold the word: `_ZB_ABORT_REASON` in this process, and the
17	# sentinel file ${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR}/.abort.signal, which crosses subshells and
18	# `_zbuild_make_fresh_shell` env scrubs (ADR-024) where a variable does not.
19	# An EMPTY sentinel reads as `sigint` — what arming wrote before it took a word.
20	#
21	# Sourced library: no `set -euo pipefail` (would mutate caller options).
22	
23	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
24	_ZBUILD_ABORT_PROP_LOADED=1
25	
26	# Empty when ZBUILD_STATE_DIR is unset: the helpers then keep the word in-process
27	# only, rather than fabricate a path under cwd.
28	_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path() {
29	    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}" ]]; then
30	        printf '%s/.abort.signal' "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR"
31	    fi
32	}
33	
34	_zbuild_abort_reason() {
35	    if [[ -n "${_ZB_ABORT_REASON:-}" ]]; then
36	        printf '%s' "$_ZB_ABORT_REASON"
37	        return 0
38	    fi
39	    local _sentinel _word=""
40	    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
41	    [[ -n "$_sentinel" && -e "$_sentinel" ]] || return 0
42	    IFS= read -r _word 2>/dev/null < "$_sentinel" || true
43	    printf '%s' "${_word:-sigint}"
44	}
45	
46	# Best-effort: a failed sentinel write must not fail a signal trap — the
47	# in-process word still holds the abort.
48	_zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel() {
49	    local _word="${1:-sigint}" _sentinel _dir _prior
50	    _prior="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"
51	    if [[ -n "$_prior" ]]; then
52	        _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_prior"
53	        return 0
54	    fi
55	    _ZB_ABORT_REASON="$_word"
56	    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
57	    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
58	    _dir="$(dirname "$_sentinel")"
59	    [[ -d "$_dir" ]] || mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
60	    printf '%s\n' "$_word" > "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
61	    return 0
62	}
63	
64	# Called by the runner's EXIT trap and by --resume, so a later run in the same
65	# state dir does not see a stale abort.
66	_zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel() {
67	    local _sentinel
68	    unset _ZB_ABORT_REASON
69	    _sentinel="$(_zbuild_abort_sentinel_path)"
70	    [[ -z "$_sentinel" ]] && return 0
71	    [[ -e "$_sentinel" ]] && rm -f "$_sentinel" 2>/dev/null || true
72	    return 0
73	}
74	
75	# Returns 1 so a caller can write `_zbuild_abort <word>; return` or `|| return 1`.
76	_zbuild_abort() {
77	    _zbuild_arm_abort_sentinel "${1:-sigint}"
78	    return 1
79	}
80	
81	_zbuild_check_abort() {
82	    [[ -n "$(_zbuild_abort_reason)" ]] && return 1
83	    return 0
84	}
85	
86	# 1 only when the child failed AND an abort is recorded: an ordinary failure is
87	# the caller's to handle, and a child that succeeded is not an abort.
88	_zbuild_propagate_abort() {
89	    [[ "${1:-0}" == "0" ]] && return 0
90	    _zbuild_check_abort
91	}
